correctness.rationale: The exact covariance-centered trace reduces to n-3+p^T B p; orientation-free unsigned incidence gives B=(1/2)I+(1/4)M^TM, hence strict convexity. The path inverse solves a second-order difference boundary problem with positive closed form for every m>=1. Uniform and boundary asymptotics follow from the explicit geometric formula. The competing spectral solution is proved by a universal linear Rayleigh quotient and a polynomial-flag eigenbasis. A standalone exact-rational verifier passed 297 assertions; these are supporting checks, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Originality is the exact finite-budget covariance-isotropic optimal edge distribution, its all-path alternating boundary layer, and the rigorous opposite ranking to a separately optimal spectral-gap design. The fully inspected key Boyd 2004 and 2006 material optimizes spectral convergence, not this two-contact trace objective. Closest published research-record claims concern deterministic Gini sweeps, synchronous full matchings, or spatially homogeneous rounds; they do not imply the claim. Semantic searches are negative evidence only and older unindexed equivalent convex-design formulations remain a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: An older exact finite-horizon Frobenius/trace or minimum-collision design for paths could be published under different terminology.
The 2004 conference manuscript has a precise public IEEE online posting on 2005-05-16; no earlier day-specific public release date was verified for the December 2004 proceedings.
Source comparisons include selected full-text sections rather than a complete census of every historical publication.

value.rationale: A natural two-contact communication-budget design is entirely degenerate at one contact, yet becomes a unique all-size nonuniform optimum at the very next contact. Its alternating endpoint profile with an exact geometric decay constant and opposite ordering to the unique spectral-gap-optimal distribution is a substantive structural finite-horizon-versus-long-horizon contrast. The effect and its precise invariant are motivated by sampling policy, not an arbitrary enumeration. The small P4 numerical gain is not offered as the sole significance.
